adapters.waits: The rail that sells nothing (apps-gov-in's `none`, a store channel with no bridge, an undeclared channel): no purchase, cancel, pending or lifetime scenario exists for it to pass. assert-purchase-path §G holds it to a literal `canStartCheckout => false` and no launcher instead.

_why: THE CLIENT HALF (port-pay-client): the Dart seams an app speaks — PurchaseRail (the rail a channel sells through) and IapBridge (the store SDK behind a store rail) — declared in packages/purchases and exported from its library file, interface.dart.

L3: every seam has two or more adapters whose conformance test CALLS its runner (packages/purchases/lib/testing/conformance.dart) with nothing pending — PurchaseRail: the hosted rail on every hosted channel, the store rail on every store channel, and the shared fake; IapBridge: RevenueCat against a fake method channel, and the shared fake. assert-ports limb 10 earns it; the rail that sells nothing waits, printed.

SELECTION is the port's: the channel row decides (selection.source). The client reads it RENDERED — tooling/ports/render.mjs writes packages/purchases/lib/src/generated/rails.dart (channel → rail kind) — so a channel changing rail is a register edit and a re-render, and no Dart names a payment vendor: every hosted-page rail is `hosted`, and which merchant serves it is the server's business.

BOTH HALVES: inbound is the webhook door (POST /v1/money/<provider>) behind [ADR 004]'s MoRWebhookVerifier, re-exported as RailInbound; outbound is RailOutbound (checkout, cancel, refund, reconcile) in services/_shared/src/ports/payments.ts. Routes reach a rail only through services/platform/src/ports.ts (railFor / inboundFor), which reads the rendered table services/platform/src/generated/ports.ts (tooling/ports/render.mjs).
